annotations.text:
ChampPreso — gate, narrate, prune

The problem isn't chrome. It's that the board draws everything it hears and explains none of it.

These wireframes match the real app: tokens, type and geometry lifted from public/style.css (ink #0B0D12, ember #FF6B35, paper #F4F4F0, 40px strip, caption pill at bottom:78px). Layout is the proposal; the styling is what already ships.

Top row = the four Listening states. Bottom row = the three surfaces being pruned.

IDLE — the state that proves the pruning.

On screen: caption (last thing heard, faded) and End. That's it. No Undo, no Interrupt, no cost drawer, no zone chip, no waveform.

The clock and the green dot stay — subtle, plain muted text, no bubble. 'Is it alive' is the complaint, and a running clock is the cheapest possible evidence.

THE GATE — the Granola standard: keep everything, draw what matters.

The canvas here is pixel-identical to idle. Nothing was drawn, and the caption says so: HEARD · NOTED FOR CONTEXT.

Gated speech is never discarded — it buffers into the next turn's context and the session review, exactly how meeting summarizers stay accurate through off-topic wander. The gate decides WHEN to draw, never what the agent gets to know.

CANDIDATE — the board shows its own confidence.

Dashed border, 50% opacity, CANDIDATE tag. Solidifies when the conversation confirms it; expires on its own if the room moves on (never if you've touched or pinned it).

The ember ring is the just-changed highlight. Caption carries heard → doing. Stop appears only because it's mid-turn.

THE TWO INVISIBLE TURNS.

Today a turn that draws nothing, and a turn that fails, look exactly like a turn that never happened. Both get words.

'Nothing worth drawing yet' is a feature working correctly. 'The model timed out. Nothing was lost.' is a failure that doesn't make you wonder what you lost.

PRUNE — kill a thread and everything under it, in one action.

Selecting a node shows what would go: 3 shapes + 2 arrows, tinted crimson. readBoardStructure() already computes this graph, so 'everything downstream' is a solved problem.

The control appears on selection and nowhere else.

SETUP — 39 controls become one question.

Everything on the left still exists: palette, restore, notes, mic, settings all move behind Options in the strip. Templates stay visible because they ARE the quick path.

DECIDED: the button says 'Start whiteboarding', and the live state label becomes 'Whiteboarding' — this is the whiteboard that whiteboards itself, and the vocabulary plays into it.

SETTINGS — 47 keys become three questions.

Left is the default view. Right is Advanced expanded, to prove nothing was lost.

The red block is the exception to 'hide, don't remove': seven settings wired to nothing. providerFallback sat in your config promising failover that did not exist. Those get deleted, not hidden.
